recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. Do not add redundant FHIR-51604 prose unless a future work-group decision, such as the still-triaged FHIR-51728, changes the broader compliant-deviation policy.
issue_request: FHIR-51604 was Applied/Persuasive with Modification for R6 and asked to clarify whether core CompartmentDefinition instances are examples or definitional, whether HL7-defined instances may be hosted elsewhere, and whether server-specific omissions or additions can be described. The approved change replaced the ambiguous 'compartment definitions' wording with 'CompartmentDefinition instances' and added that there is no computable mechanism for describing a given server's compartment implementation.
initial_application: Git commit e2bdd38ac37317d87d2264118e39cd7c5fc06d24 explicitly applied FHIR-51604 to source/compartmentdefinition/compartmentdefinition-introduction.xml. The current source still carries the HL7-only CompartmentDefinition-instance clarification and the server-implementation mechanism statement.
additional_context: source/fhir.ini shows compartmentdefinition is an active, approved resource/page artifact. FHIR-I minutes on 2025-08-11 record the persuasive 11-0-0 vote. The motivating Zulip thread raised the same examples-versus-definitions and server-deviation ambiguity. Later applied issue FHIR-51725 changed adjacent text, added listed-resource/.param expectations, and changed 'no computable mechanism' to 'no mechanism', which is a same-family refinement rather than a missing FHIR-51604 application. FHIR-51607 and FHIR-51725 are already represented on the combined branch; FHIR-51728 remains unresolved.
reconciliation: No source edit was made. The current active source says CompartmentDefinition instances can only be defined by HL7 International in this specification, may be hosted on other servers, and cannot be used to describe a given server's compartment implementation; adjacent later text explains listed resources and additional-resource handling.
